name: onesie-setup
description: Use when onesie is not on PATH, when no API key resolves, when the session start hook reports either, or when the user asks how to install or set up onesie. Walks the user through installing it, choosing a provider and storing a key, without the key ever entering the conversation.
compatibility: Needs a shell, and Homebrew or a Go toolchain to install onesie.

rules.short: Never ask for the key in chat. The user stores it with onesie auth set, outside the conversation.
rules.why: Anything typed into the conversation is sent to the model and kept in the transcript. `onesie auth set` reads the key from a hidden prompt in a real terminal, or from the first line of stdin, and never prints it. So ask the user to run `onesie auth set` in their own terminal, or to pipe it from a password manager, as in `pass show typesafe | onesie auth set`. A command that reads from a password manager is safe to run for them, since only the path it wrote comes back.

rules.short: Ask which account the user has, TypeSafe or OpenRouter, before storing a key.
rules.why: typesafe is the default. For openrouter, store the key with `onesie --provider openrouter auth set`, and have the user add `export ONESIE_PROVIDER=openrouter` to their shell profile. Otherwise every command needs `--provider openrouter`, and without it onesie looks for a TypeSafe key and reports none.

rules.short: End the setup with onesie auth test, not auth status.
rules.why: `auth status` only reports where a key would come from. `auth test` sends it to the provider's model listing, which costs no tokens, and exits 3 when the key is refused. Only a clean `auth test` means the next real command will work.
